title: Malavika Mohanan's Chennai Food Diary: Dosa, Podi Idli, and Four Chutneys at a Mylapore Favourite
excerpt: The actress shared her go-to South Indian breakfast spot — Haritam in Mylapore — where a plate of crispy dosa comes with an arsenal of homemade chutneys.
body:
• Actress Malavika Mohanan shared an Instagram carousel of a South Indian breakfast at Haritam restaurant in Mylapore, Chennai.
  • The spread featured crispy dosa with four chutneys — coconut, tomato-onion, peanut, and green — alongside podi idli with sambar.
  • Haritam is known for its old-world charm and traditional South Indian fare in one of Chennai's most historic neighborhoods.

When Malavika Mohanan has a day in Chennai, she heads straight for the classics. The actress recently shared a carousel of photos on Instagram documenting a breakfast stop at Haritam, a restaurant in Mylapore that she called her "absolute favourite" in the city, according to NDTV Food.

The Spread

"Cute place, yum food, old world charm," Mohanan's caption read."

The images showed Mohanan posing with a plate of crispy dosa accompanied by four small sides: coconut chutney, tomato-onion chutney, peanut chutney, and green chutney. Alongside it sat a plate of podi idli — bite-sized steamed rice cakes tossed in traditional South Indian spice powder with aromatic curry leaves, served with a small metal bowl of sambar on the side.

The setup is a textbook South Indian breakfast — nothing fussy, nothing reinvented, just good dosa with proper accompaniments. The four-chutney lineup is what sets a quality restaurant apart from the ordinary: each brings a different texture and flavor profile to the same dosa, from the creamy mildness of coconut to the heat of the green chutney.

About Haritam

Haritam sits in Mylapore, one of Chennai's oldest neighborhoods and a cultural heartland known for the Kapaleeshwarar Temple, silk shops, and a dense concentration of traditional South Indian restaurants. The area draws both locals and visitors looking for authentic Chennai flavors without the polish of hotel dining.

"A day in Chennai. P.S at my absolute favourite restaurant — Haritam. Cute place, yum food, old world charm," Mohanan's caption read.

Why It Matters for Diaspora Foodies

For NRIs planning a Chennai visit, Mylapore remains the neighborhood to bookmark for traditional South Indian breakfast. Haritam's combination of classic dosa, handmade chutneys, and podi idli in an intimate setting is the kind of experience that chains and hotel restaurants rarely replicate. The restaurant's old-world atmosphere — quiet, unpretentious, focused on the food — is exactly what many diaspora travelers say they miss most about eating in India.
